# Flags and reasons

Every flag, note, score, and reason *hxex* writes into its tables: what it means, what *hxex* does about it, and what to look at. Thresholds are given at their defaults; `hxex explain NAME --project hxex.toml` gives them with your project's settings, and `hxex explain` lists them all. The `flags.csv` beside the tables (`hxex report`) and in each analysis folder (`hxex analyse`) lists the ones that occur in those results, with how often and the thresholds they were judged by.

## Quality flags

Marks on single spectra (and on every spectrum of a series, for the checks of a whole series), in the `flags` column of `spectra.csv` and the overview. A flag alone leaves nothing out; the analysis acts on `off_mz` and `undeut_high` (see each).

| Name | Where | Meaning | What *hxex* does | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`poor_fit`](outputs.md#quality-flags) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | The fit is much worse than the other fits of its series. The misfit relative to the spectrum's own intensity is more than `poor_fit_factor` (10) times its series' median, and the deviance is above `min_deviance` (1). Judged only in series with at least `min_series_fits` (5) fitted spectra. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Look at the spectrum and its fit: another species, a spike, or a peak the picking cut. |
| [`low_intensity`](outputs.md#quality-flags) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | Far less signal than the other replicates at the same time point. The total intensity is below `min_intensity` (0.3) of the other replicates' mean, once each injection's overall brightness is divided out (an injection that is dim throughout is named in a warning and in `hxex info`, not flagged spectrum by spectrum). Spectra without replicates are not judged. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | A weak spectrum's fit is noisier: compare it with its replicates. |
| [`noise_outlier`](outputs.md#quality-flags) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | A replicate the replicate-based noise estimate left out. | A control replicate is also left out of its control's average (the series then has `m0_replicate_left_out` or `fd_replicate_left_out`). | Compare it with its replicates. |
| [`mz_shift`](outputs.md#quality-flags) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (series, on each of its spectra) | The series' peaks sit off their predicted m/z. The series' peaks are, as a rule, more than `max_mz_offset_ppm` (15) ppm from where the composition puts them, compared with the run as a whole. Judged only for series `off_mz` does not check: fragment ions, and series without an undeuterated control. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | A wrong sequence, modification, terminus, or ion type, or another species. |
| [`off_mz`](picking-window.md#a-series-whose-peaks-sit-off-its-mz) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (series, on each of its spectra) | The series' undeuterated peaks sit further from the run's calibration than its other series: most likely another species. The limit is `off_mz_sd` (6) times the run's scatter. Often the retention time points at another peptide of almost the same mass. | `hxex analyse` leaves the series out (`off_mz = true`; reason `off its m/z`), controls included. | Check the retention time in the peptide table (`find_retention_time` can suggest one). |
| [`rt_found`](inputs.md#when-the-peptide-tables-time-is-wrong) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (series, on each of its spectra) | The series was read at the retention time found for its exact m/z, not the peptide table's. Set by `find_retention_time = "automatic"` in `[input.scans]`. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Check the time in `retention_suggestions.csv` and correct the peptide table. |
| [`drift_unclear`](inputs.md#ion-mobility-each-peptides-drift-time) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (series, on each of its spectra) | The series was read from ion mobility files without a clear drift-time range. No undeuterated control had signal (every drift time was summed), or the undeuterated drift profile has a second peak the isotope spacing cannot tell apart, or the tallest drift peak sat off the peptide's m/z while another sat on it (that one was used; the log names both). | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Look at its spectra, or give the peptide its own `drift_start` and `drift_end`. |
| [`elution_cut`](inputs.md#finding-each-fragment-channels-peak) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | A fragment spectrum whose elution peak reaches the first or last scan recorded for its precursor. The acquisition missed part of the peak (`find_fragment_peak`), so the spectrum is dimmer than it should be. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Retention moved in that run: check the scheduled window. |
| [`precursor_off`](experiments.md#fragments) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (series, on each of its spectra) | The precursor read in the fragment scans differs from its parent's MS1 spectrum by more than `max_precursor_offset` (1) D. Most likely another species in the isolation window shares its m/z. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Treat the series' fragments with care. |
| [`overlapping_ion`](experiments.md#fragments) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | Another ion of the same fragment scans puts at least `max_ion_overlap` (0.2) of this fragment's picked intensity on its bins. Their peaks are too close for the instrument to separate, so the fragment's envelope is partly the other ion's. `overlapping_ion_with` in `spectra.csv` names it and its share. Ions that are not read (a, b, and y ions), and an ion on every one of the fragment's strong bins (it cannot be told apart), are not counted. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Prefer another ion type or charge for the same residues. |
| [`below_noise`](inputs.md#fitting-fragment-ions-through-the-cut) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | A fragment spectrum fitted through the per-scan cut whose tallest peak is below `min_signal_to_noise` (4) times its scan's recorded noise. So many of its peaks were deleted scan by scan that even the fit through the cut cannot recover its deuteration. `signal_to_noise` in `spectra.csv` gives the size. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Do not rely on its value. |
| [`poor_envelope`](experiments.md#fragments) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (series, on each of its spectra) | The fragment's ion-type envelope could not be measured well. Left with one ion type's theory for want of usable reference spectra, or the measured envelope does not describe the spectra: the deuteration can be off by up to a hydrogen. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | — |
| [`saturated`](outputs.md#very-bright-spectra-saturated-tails_low-and-bright) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | An undeuterated control whose peaks beside the tallest read higher than natural abundance predicts: the tallest peak reads low, the usual sign of detector saturation. Above `saturated_ratio` (1.15) times the prediction, in most of the series' control replicates; only the brighter half of the run's undeuterated controls is judged. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Check the series' corrected uptake against the peptide's other charge states. |
| [`tails_low`](outputs.md#very-bright-spectra-saturated-tails_low-and-bright) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | An undeuterated control whose small isotope peaks read lower than natural abundance predicts. Below `tails_low_ratio` (0.7) times the prediction; seen in bright spectra, cause unknown. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | — |
| [`bright`](outputs.md#very-bright-spectra-saturated-tails_low-and-bright) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | A labelled spectrum or fully deuterated control at least as bright as a control of its series flagged `saturated` or `tails_low`. Its own shape cannot be checked, so it is marked as likely distorted in the same way. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | When two populations appear only in the brightest replicate, look at the dimmer ones. |
| [`undeut_high`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `spectra.csv` `flags` (spectrum) | An undeuterated spectrum whose mean is above `m0_max` (0.5) deuterons: another species or a wrong pick. An undeuterated peptide sits near 0. Judged spectrum by spectrum, so without replicates too. | Left out of the control's mean when the series has a good undeuterated spectrum (the series is noted `m0_replicate_left_out`), and then out of the analysis's undeuterated values; when every one is above, the series is `m0_high`. | Look at the spectrum; mark it `accepted` to keep it. |

## Control flags

Why a series' undeuterated or fully deuterated value is what it is, in `series.csv`: the `controls` column names the reasons when a stand-in was used (`control_fallback` true), `control_notes` the warnings that leave the control in use.

| Name | Where | Meaning | What *hxex* does | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`uncorrected`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | A series the controls leave as measured, such as a fragment ion. | No back-exchange correction; its values are in deuterons as measured. | — |
| [`m0_missing`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series has no undeuterated control; its undeuterated value is taken as 0 (natural abundance). | A stand-in (`control_fallback`), but a fair one: the analysis keeps the series. | — |
| [`m0_high`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The undeuterated control's mean is above `m0_max` (0.5) deuterons, so it is rejected and 0 is used. Most often another species of almost the same m/z sits in the picking windows, usually in the labelled spectra too. | A stand-in (`control_fallback`): `hxex analyse` leaves the series out with `stand_in_controls = "exclude"` (reason `stand-in control (undeuterated)`). | Look at the undeuterated spectra; mark them `accepted` to keep the series. |
| [`m0_unreplicated`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The undeuterated control has one replicate, so its value has no uncertainty. | None: the control is used. | — |
| [`fd_unreplicated`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control has one replicate, so its value has no uncertainty. | None: the control is used. | — |
| [`no_amides`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The peptide has no exchangeable amides, so no fully deuterated value can scale it. | A stand-in is used. | — |
| [`fd_missing`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series has no fully deuterated control. | It takes the next value in the order (another charge state, another sample, the map, or the run-wide value). | — |
| [`retention_low`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control's retention is 0 or less, or below `retention_min` (off): it is rejected. | It takes the next value in the order. | Look at the control's spectra. |
| [`retention_high`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control's retention is above `retention_max` (1.1): it cannot be right, so it is rejected. | It takes the next value in the order. | Look at the control's spectra: another species, or a wrong pick. |
| [`fd_below_data`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control is below the highest time point of its series: the sample did not fully deuterate, so it is rejected. A little below is allowed (`time_course_tolerance` (0.1) D per amide); each time point counts by the median of its replicates. | It takes the next value in the order. | — |
| [`retention_outlier`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control's retention is far below the run's other controls, so it is rejected. More than `outlier_sd` (4) robust standard deviations below their median; made only with at least ten accepted controls and no `retention_min`. | It takes the next value in the order. | — |
| [`fd_off_model`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control misses the retention predicted from the peptide's sequence by more than `kint_tolerance` (0.15) per amide, so it is rejected. Only with the quench conditions given (`quench` in `[run.controls]`). | It takes the next value in the order. | — |
| [`fd_charges_combined`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series' fully deuterated value is the mean retention of the peptide's accepted controls over its charge states. Set by `combine_charges = true`: retention belongs to the peptide, not its charge. | Counts as measured: not a stand-in. | — |
| [`fd_other_charge`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series has no good fully deuterated control of its own and takes the peptide's controls at its other charge states. | Counts as measured when charge states are combined (the default); a stand-in with `combine_charges = false`. | — |
| [`fd_other_sample`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series takes the same peptide's fully deuterated controls in the run's other samples. Close to the peptide's own: the samples of one run share the peptide and the LC. | A stand-in (`control_fallback`): `hxex analyse` leaves the series out with `stand_in_controls = "exclude"` (reason `stand-in control`); `other_sample` keeps these. | — |
| [`fd_map`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series takes a retention map of the overlapping peptides with accepted controls. | A stand-in (`control_fallback`): `hxex analyse` leaves the series out with `stand_in_controls = "exclude"` (reason `stand-in control`). | — |
| [`fd_median`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series takes the median retention of the run's accepted controls. | A stand-in (`control_fallback`): `hxex analyse` leaves the series out with `stand_in_controls = "exclude"` (reason `stand-in control`). | — |
| [`fd_kint`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The series takes the retention predicted from its sequence, fitted to the run's accepted controls. Only with the quench conditions given (`quench` in `[run.controls]`). | A stand-in (`control_fallback`): `hxex analyse` leaves the series out with `stand_in_controls = "exclude"` (reason `stand-in control`). | — |
| [`fd_disagrees`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | The same peptide's fully deuterated controls in the other samples have a clearly different retention. By more than `sample_tolerance` (0.1); in one run they should agree closely. | A warning: the control is still used. | Look at the control's spectra in each sample. |
| [`fd_multimodal`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | Most of the fully deuterated control's replicates were fitted best with more than one population. `series.csv` adds whether its retention agrees with the other samples' (`retention agrees`, `retention differs`), with its other charge states', or was not checked (`retention unchecked`). Differing can mean an incompletely deuterated sample. | A warning: the control's average is still used. | With `retention unchecked` or `retention differs`, look at its spectra. |
| [`fd_retention_agrees`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control's retention agrees with the same peptide's in the other samples. | None: written as `fd_multimodal (retention agrees)` in `control_notes`. | — |
| [`fd_charges_agree`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `controls` (series) | The fully deuterated control's retention agrees with the peptide's other charge states. | None: written as `fd_multimodal (retention agrees with its other charge states)` in `control_notes`. | — |
| [`m0_multimodal`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | Most of the undeuterated control's replicates were fitted best with more than one population. An undeuterated sample has one population, so another species may be there. | A warning: the control is still used. | Look at the undeuterated spectra. |
| [`data_below_m0`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | A time point of the series reads below its undeuterated control. By more than `time_course_tolerance` (0.1) D per amide. The early time points are the hardest to measure, so it is the time point that is suspect. | A warning: the control is still used. | Look at that time point's spectra. |
| [`fd_charges_disagree`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | The peptide's charge states, whose fully deuterated controls are combined, differ in retention by more than `sample_tolerance` (0.1). | A warning: the combined value is still used. | — |
| [`m0_replicate_left_out`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | An undeuterated control replicate was left out of the average. Above `m0_max` beside a good one (`undeut_high`), above the amide count, far from the other replicates (`replicate_outlier` (6) typical standard deviations), or a noise outlier. | The control is the mean of the others. | — |
| [`fd_replicate_left_out`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | A fully deuterated control replicate was left out of the average. Above the amide count, far from the other replicates (`replicate_outlier` (6) typical standard deviations), or a noise outlier. | The control is the mean of the others. | — |
| [`fd_deamidated`](back-exchange-correction.md#deamidated-fully-deuterated-controls) | `series.csv` `control_notes` (series) | The fully deuterated control was lowered by its sample's deamidated share. Only with `deamidation = false`, for a peptide holding an Asn-Gly site; `deamidated_share` in `series.csv` gives the share. | The lowered value is the series' own, measured control. | — |

## Population test flags

Signs that an extra population may be another species, or that more populations may be there, from the population test (`[run.population_test]`). Flags only: no number of populations changes.

| Name | Where | Meaning | What *hxex* does | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`narrow_component`](population-test.md#two-flags-for-other-species) | `spectra.csv` `narrow_component` (spectrum) | The fit at the spectrum's number of populations has a population narrower than deuterium allows. The narrowest width is set by the peptide's amides and the D2O fraction (`d2o_fraction` (0.9)). Much narrower may be another species, or a spike. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | Look at the spectrum. |
| [`undeuterated_two`](population-test.md#two-flags-for-other-species) | `species_uptake.csv` `undeuterated_two` (peptide, on every row in every sample) | The peptide's undeuterated spectra read two populations: something else is there. Whether the labelled spectra share the other species is not known. | Flag only, unless `undeuterated_cap = false`: the peptide's labelled spectra then stay at one population. | Look at the undeuterated spectra. |
| [`more_populations_possible`](population-test.md#turning-it-on) | `spectra.csv` and `species_uptake.csv` `more_populations_possible` (spectrum, and peptide and time) | The test's quick step above `decide_up_to` would add a population. Set with `decide_up_to = off`; a run that decides more populations tells. | Flag only: nothing is left out or changed. | — |

## Spectrum quality screens

Scores from 0 to 1, in the last columns of `spectra.csv`: the share of the intensity that looks like another species. `hxex analyse` acts on them by `[analysis.filters] spectrum_quality_filtering` (`loose`, the default, `strict`, or `none`).

| Name | Where | Meaning | What *hxex* does | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`screen_below_mono`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `spectra.csv` `screen_below_mono` (spectrum) | Another species starting below the peptide's lightest peak, whose isotope peaks carry on into the peptide's. The share of the peptide's peaks that this carry-on explains. Empty when the spectrum does not reach far enough below the peptide. | `hxex analyse` leaves the spectrum out from 0.1 at `loose` and 0.05 at `strict`. | — |
| [`screen_off_position`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `spectra.csv` `screen_off_position` (spectrum) | Intensity of the five lowest peaks found away from where the composition puts them. An overlapping species of slightly different mass does this. | `hxex analyse` leaves the spectrum out from 0.2 at `loose` and 0.1 at `strict`. | — |
| [`screen_between`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `spectra.csv` `screen_between` (spectrum) | Peaks between the isotope positions, inside or touching the peptide's envelope. Another species, often of another charge. | `hxex analyse` leaves the spectrum out from 0.4 at `loose` and 0.2 at `strict`. | — |
| [`screen_between_separate`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `spectra.csv` `screen_between_separate` (spectrum) | Peaks between the isotope positions in a cluster of their own above the envelope. The fit could take the cluster for a second, more deuterated population. | `hxex analyse` keeps the spectrum at one population from 0.2 at `loose` and 0.1 at `strict`. | — |
| [`screen_beyond_reach`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `spectra.csv` `screen_beyond_reach` (spectrum) | Intensity beyond the heaviest the peptide can be. Those peaks belong to something else; when most of the intensity lies there, the spectrum is mostly another species. | `hxex analyse` warns from 0.1 at `loose` and 0.1 at `strict` and leaves the spectrum out from 0.5 at `loose` and 0.3 at `strict`. | — |

## Reasons a spectrum is left out

The `reason` column of `left_out_spectra.csv` in an analysis folder, and the window's "left out" column. Marking a spectrum `accepted` in the user review table keeps it against every one of these.

| Name | Where | Meaning | What *hxex* does | What to look at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`off its m/z`](picking-window.md#a-series-whose-peaks-sit-off-its-mz) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (series) | The series is flagged `off_mz`: most likely another species. | Left out by `off_mz = true`, controls included. | — |
| [`spectrum quality (screen_below_mono)`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | The spectrum's `screen_below_mono` score reached the level's threshold. | Left out by `spectrum_quality_filtering = "loose"` (from 0.1 at `loose` and 0.05 at `strict`); a control left out is also left out of the correction. | — |
| [`spectrum quality (screen_off_position)`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | The spectrum's `screen_off_position` score reached the level's threshold. | Left out by `spectrum_quality_filtering = "loose"` (from 0.2 at `loose` and 0.1 at `strict`); a control left out is also left out of the correction. | — |
| [`spectrum quality (screen_between)`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | The spectrum's `screen_between` score reached the level's threshold. | Left out by `spectrum_quality_filtering = "loose"` (from 0.4 at `loose` and 0.2 at `strict`); a control left out is also left out of the correction. | — |
| [`spectrum quality (screen_beyond_reach)`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | The spectrum's `screen_beyond_reach` score reached the level's threshold. | Left out by `spectrum_quality_filtering = "loose"` (from 0.5 at `loose` and 0.3 at `strict`); a control left out is also left out of the correction. | — |
| [`kept at K = 1 (spectrum quality)`](outputs.md#spectrum-quality-screens) | the window's "left out" column (spectrum) | The spectrum's `screen_between_separate` score reached the level's threshold: it is kept with one population only. | Not left out, and not counted as left out. | — |
| [`undeuterated control above m0_max`](back-exchange-correction.md#how-hxex-judges-the-controls) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | An undeuterated spectrum flagged `undeut_high` that the controls left out of their mean. | Left out of the analysis's undeuterated values. | — |
| [`undeuterated replicate the controls left out`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | An undeuterated replicate the controls left out of their mean (far from the others, above the amide count, or a noise outlier). | Left out of the analysis's undeuterated values. | — |
| [`stand-in control`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (series) | The series' fully deuterated value is a stand-in, not a measurement. On a large dataset these were the series most often corrected above full deuteration. | Left out by `stand_in_controls = "exclude"`, except in a sample with no measured fully deuterated control at all. | — |
| [`stand-in control (screened)`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (series) | The spectrum quality screens left out every measured fully deuterated control of the series, so only a stand-in was left. | Left out by `stand_in_controls = "exclude"`. | — |
| [`stand-in control (undeuterated)`](back-exchange-correction.md#the-order-of-the-values) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (series) | The series' undeuterated control was rejected as too heavy (`m0_high`). Replacing its value by 0 fixes the start, but the other species is still in its labelled spectra. | Left out by `stand_in_controls = "exclude"`, in every sample; `hxex analyse` warns when half a sample's series or more go this way. | A long peptide just over the limit can be good: mark its spectra `accepted` to keep it. |
| [`above the amide count`](statistics.md#seeing-what-was-left-out) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | The spectrum's one-population mean is above the peptide's amide count: impossible for the peptide alone. | Left out by `above_amides = true`. | — |
| [`replicate outlier`](statistics.md#seeing-what-was-left-out) | `left_out_spectra.csv` `reason` (spectrum) | The spectrum lies far from its replicates at the same time point. | Left out by `replicate_outlier = 6` (typical replicate standard deviations), with three or more replicates. | — |
